skill.name: s3-upload-handler
skill.description: Guide implementation of AWS S3 uploads with UI components, client upload logic, and server-side processing.
skill.summary: Adds practical S3 upload guidance for web apps using presigned upload flows.
skill.author: AayushBaniya2006

security_audit.summary: Most external-command findings are false positives from Markdown inline code and fenced TypeScript examples, with no shell execution. The AWS credential and .env.local guidance is confirmed as sensitive secret handling, and the presigned upload example adds a high-risk concern because it lacks visible access control and uses public-read uploads.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer managed AWS credentials, short-lived roles, or deployment platform secrets. Warn agents not to read, print, or commit .env.local values.

remediation.issue: The presigned upload route omits authentication and authorization.
remediation.suggestion: Require an authenticated user, authorize the upload prefix, bind keys to an owner, and reject requests outside the allowed tenant or account scope.

remediation.issue: The example allows client-controlled file type and public-read objects.
remediation.suggestion: Validate MIME type and extension on the server, use private object ACLs, and serve files through signed read URLs or a controlled CDN policy.

remediation.issue: The S3 key includes the original file name from the request.
remediation.suggestion: Normalize file names, reject path separators and unsafe characters, and generate server-controlled object keys for each upload.

content.user_title: Add S3 Uploads to Your App
content.value_statement: Building file uploads takes UI, client logic, and server routes. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through S3 upload patterns for web apps.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use the S3Uploader component for button or dropzone uploads.
Shows how ClientS3Uploader supports custom client-side upload interfaces.
Describes server-side uploads for generated or processed files.
Lists S3Uploader props such as maxFiles, maxSize, accept, multiple, value, and onChange.
Provides an AWS SDK presigned post route example for browser uploads.
Identifies required AWS environment configuration for region and bucket settings.
limitations: The skill package contains guidance and references, not the referenced implementation source files.
Projects still need an AWS account, S3 bucket, IAM policy, and required SDK packages.
Authentication, authorization, validation, and private access controls must be added by the developer.
The examples assume TypeScript, React, and Next.js style project structure.

use_cases.title: Add User Avatar Uploads
use_cases.description: Use the button variant to guide a simple single-file upload flow for profile images.

use_cases.title: Build Project File Dropzones
use_cases.description: Use the dropzone pattern with file count and size limits for multi-file workflows.

use_cases.title: Upload Generated Server Files
use_cases.description: Use the server utility pattern when API routes or server actions create files before storage.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Upload
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a standard page upload.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a simple S3 upload flow for a Next.js page. Recommend the component, required props, and setup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Customize Upload UI
prompt_templates.scenario: Custom client interface with a hidden file input or branded button.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a custom S3 upload interface with ClientS3Uploader. Include state handling, progress expectations, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Add Server Uploads
prompt_templates.scenario: Server-side generation or processing before storage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a server-side S3 upload path for generated files. Include content type, object path, and response handling.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Presigned Uploads
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of security controls for production uploads.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review a presigned S3 upload route. Identify missing authentication, authorization, validation, object ACL, and key naming controls.

output_examples.input: Add a profile image uploader to my account settings page.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends the button variant, lists the required route and callback, and notes where to store the returned image URL.

output_examples.input: I need a project asset dropzone with five files and image-only uploads.
output_examples.output: The assistant describes the dropzone configuration, file limits, accepted image types, and expected upload completion behavior.

output_examples.input: Review my presigned upload route before production.
output_examples.output: The assistant reports missing access checks, server-side validation needs, private object storage recommendations, and safer object key handling.

best_practices: Use least-privilege IAM permissions and deployment platform secrets for AWS access.
Validate file size, MIME type, extension, ownership, and object key prefix on the server.
Keep uploaded objects private by default and grant read access through signed URLs or controlled delivery.
anti_patterns: Do not expose long-lived AWS credentials in prompts, logs, code, or committed environment files.
Do not trust client-provided fileName, fileType, or upload path without server validation.
Do not use public-read uploads unless the product explicitly requires public objects.

faq.question: Does this skill include the S3 uploader source code?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and references to expected component and utility files.

faq.question: Which upload patterns does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers a React UI component, a custom client uploader, and a server-side upload helper.

faq.question: Can it help with presigned URLs?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a presigned post route example using the AWS SDK.

faq.question: Is the example production ready?
faq.answer: No. Production routes need authentication, authorization, validation, private object access, and safer key generation.

faq.question: What tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What project style does it assume?
faq.answer: It assumes a TypeScript web app with React components and Next.js style API routes.
